title: Lay Out the Cookbook — tested recipes to heirloom pages
objective: Measure whether the cookbook-layout craftbook assembles the seeded recipe shelf into a print-ready book: every tested recipe in its chapter with its provenance line, untested recipes listed at the back, family phrasings preserved.
prompt: i think weve got enough tested recipes — can you lay out the cookbok? one per grandchild eventually so make it printable

setup.about: Family recipe book project for the Van Daalens. The recipe index is workspace/recipes.json with one markdown file per recipe under workspace/recipes; the laid-out book goes under workspace/book.
setup.missionObjectives: Tested recipes go in with their provenance intact; untested ones are listed for the next round, never silently dropped. Everything is grounded in the shelf — no live services, no real credentials.

# Oma Trudy's Split Pea Soup

Oma Trudy's — came over from Groningen in 1954.

## Ingredients
- 500 g split peas
- 1 smoked sausage (the good one, not the budget one — Oma's margin note)
- 2 leeks, 1 celeriac, 2 carrots
- a ham hock

## Method
Soak the peas while you argue about whether soaking is necessary. Simmer everything except the sausage for two hours until 'a spoon stands up in it'. Add the sausage for the last twenty minutes. Better tomorrow than today.

# Saturday Brown Bread

Grandpa Wim's — baked every Saturday for thirty years.

## Ingredients
- 400 g wholemeal flour, 100 g rye
- 7 g yeast, 10 g salt, a knob of butter
- 350 ml warm water

## Method
Knead until your arms complain, then five minutes more. Rise under the tea towel with the blue stripe (any towel works; the blue stripe is tradition). Bake at 220 until it sounds hollow when you knock on the bottom.

# Aunt Willa's Chicken Pot Pie

Aunt Willa's — the funeral casserole that became a birthday request.

## Ingredients
- 1 whole chicken, poached and picked
- carrots, peas, pearl onions
- double crust, all butter, no shortcuts

## Method
Make the gravy from the poaching broth and do not rush it. Fill, lid, crimp with a fork the way Willa did — three presses, turn, three presses. Vent with her initials if you're feeling brave. Bake until deep gold.

# Midsummer Strawberry Cake

Mom's — invented the summer the freezer broke.

## Ingredients
- 250 g flour, 200 g sugar, 3 eggs, 200 g butter
- a full kilo of strawberries, no apologies
- whipped cream, double what seems sensible

## Method
Bake the sponge, split it while warm. Sugar the berries and let them bleed a little. Assemble taller than is structurally wise. Eat outside or it doesn't count.

# Pa's Campfire Chili

Pa's — written on the inside of a matchbook, translated by Ria.

## Ingredients
- 1 kg beef chuck, cut rough
- two onions, 'more garlic than the recipe says'
- dried anchos, a bottle of dark beer, a square of dark chocolate

## Method
Brown the beef in batches and don't crowd the pot — the matchbook underlines this twice. Low fire, three hours, stir when you think of it. The chocolate goes in at the end and you tell nobody.

# Lemon Custard for Sick Days

Oma Trudy's — the one that fixed every flu since 1962.

## Ingredients
- 500 ml whole milk
- 3 yolks, 80 g sugar, 30 g cornstarch
- zest of two lemons, juice of one

## Method
Warm the milk with the zest. Whisk yolks, sugar, and cornstarch, then marry them slowly so nothing scrambles. Thicken on low until it coats the spoon. Serve warm, in the yellow bowl if the patient is under twelve.

# The Contested Oliebollen

Disputed between Ria and Aunt Willa — two versions exist and neither yields.

## Status
Not yet tested side by side. The New Year's bake-off will settle it. Both versions are filed with the arbitration notes.

# Maple Walnut Fudge

From a fair stall in 1998 — nobody has dared it yet.

## Status
Untested. The card says 'soft-ball stage' with no thermometer number, which is why it has waited twenty-eight years.
